rich_summary: Narada recounts the devastation caused by the Asura brothers Sunda and Upasunda. Having gained immense power, they roam the world in shifting forms—elephants, lions, and tigers—hunting down sages and destroying sacred life. Sacrifices cease, trade stops, agriculture is abandoned, and the earth becomes a desolate field of bones. The gods, sages, and celestial beings, distressed by the collapse of cosmic order, appeal to Brahma for a solution. Brahma devises a subtle strategy: he orders the divine craftsman Viswakarman to create a woman of incomparable beauty. From the finest features of all creation emerges Tilottama, a celestial maiden whose beauty captivates even the gods. Her task is to enchant the inseparable brothers so that rivalry and desire will cause them to destroy each other, restoring balance to the world.

highlight_spans.why: A vivid opening depicting the destruction of sacred spaces and the collapse of cosmic order under the Asura brothers.
Shows the demons' terrifying shapeshifting hunts and the extermination of sages, marking the peak of their tyranny.
The gathering of gods and sages before Brahma highlights the cosmic scale of the crisis and the appeal to divine governance.
Brahma orders the creation of a captivating maiden—this decision introduces the clever, nonviolent strategy to defeat the demons.
The description and naming of Tilottama emphasize her symbolic construction from the finest elements of beauty in the universe.
The moment when even the gods are entranced by Tilottama, causing Shiva to manifest multiple faces and Indra many eyes, underscores her overwhelming allure.

top_scenes.scene_text: The demon brothers Sunda and Upasunda roam a devastated earth in monstrous forms, while ruined temples and scattered bones cover the desolate landscape.
Viswakarman presents Tilottama—an impossibly radiant celestial maiden formed from the finest gems and features—to Brahma in a luminous divine court.
Tilottama circles the assembly of gods as Shiva sprouts faces in every direction and Indra gains a thousand eyes to behold her beauty.
